items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: The interviewee discusses listening to recordings of Basie and Goodman, mentioning they are 'great artists' and listing personnel, but describes no personal interaction, meeting, or professional collaboration with Basie or Goodman himself.

ctx.x: It was awful. The tape that was made in the 70s especially. When you went back it just started shredding and you’d stop. So we were literally putting them in little ovens, and we called it baking the tapes to keep them from just flaking — you know if you ran it through one time it was gone. There was all the oxide laying on the table. So one of the guys got the idea that baking them — and now they do it — it’s very sophisticated. But I started listening — I was kind of skeptical when I saw those tapes and I put…
When they cut those solos out then they were splicing tape?
